analysis.title: US Market Intell Afternoon Briefing
key_insights: Fed held rates on Oct 28 with two dissents (Cook, Hammack), in line with expectations. Warsh's press conference held no surprises, and OIS markets still price about 85% odds of a December hike. Treasury yields steepened (2Y -6bp, 10Y/30Y flat to +2bp).

Market Intel calls the Fed hold a dovish outcome, since growth has likely accelerated to an above-trend pace. The last 2 Flash PMIs point to about 5% real GDP growth with rising inflationary inputs. One explanation offered is the focus on incremental financial conditions tightening, mainly via credit markets, as a reason for fewer hikes.

US stocks closed higher (SPX +0.3%, NDX +0.5%, RTY +0.4%) but breadth was slightly negative. SPW was flat and Mag 7 were mostly lower. AI themes led: SK Hynix (SKHY) posted a big beat with longer demand visibility, and APH, FLEX, STX and VRT gave strong commentary.
ORCL rose 11% after its analyst day, on a stronger FY30 free cash flow guide.
Input cost pressure is a key theme outside tech. Transports and Packaging lagged on companies' price hike plans and comments on cost pressure.

MSFT is up 5% after hours. Azure beat buyside estimates by 1 point and operating income beat by 5%. JPM's Mark Schilsky says the Q2 FY27 Azure guide needs to be at least +48% Y/Y FXN at the high end to sustain bulls' belief in +50% growth.

GOOGL is down 7% after hours on what JPM calls a straight miss. Search missed buyside estimates by 2% despite the highest query growth in 5 years, because pricing is declining faster than investors expected. YouTube and Google Cloud revenue also missed, though Cloud operating margins were strong, and consolidated operating income missed.
NOW is down 15% after hours. CRPO missed buyside estimates and the Q4 CRPO guide implies a 250bp sequential deceleration. Investor sentiment going into the print was a touch long.

Earnings read-through on labor is mixed. ADP reported fiscal Q1 pays per control growth of 2%, ahead of expectations, and raised its fiscal 2027 outlook to about 1% from 0-1%. Skilled labor remains a recurring theme.
ODFL and CHRW, both sub-$50bn companies, plan to cut headcount while core volumes grow. JPM reads this as automation and efficiency gains weakening the link between business growth and labor demand.

Wage inflation remains a concern, especially for sub-$50bn companies. Benefits and healthcare costs have pushed total employment expenses higher. ODFL's fringe benefit rate was 42.8% in Q3 versus 39.7% a year earlier.

AI infrastructure demand is accelerating. GEV's backlog rose from $176bn to about $200bn with almost $30bn of new orders in Q3. VRT's Q3 data center orders were up more than 100% organically Y/Y, and its EMEA pipeline roughly doubled.

US Market Intel remains Tactically Bullish. SPX lost 2.4% over two weeks and is -36bp month to date, with 8 of 11 sectors positive. About a quarter of SPX has reported, with no dips to pre-season forecasts (about 13% revenue growth, 30% EPS growth, 15% margins).
Sentiment is firmly in the Fear region, but there has not been a complete positioning washout, so the signal is less clear.

Geopolitical risk is the primary risk. Iran has indicated it would likely target Saudi and UAE energy infrastructure with the SPR at multi-decade lows. The worst case is escalation with Russian refining capacity hit again. Market Intel buys Tech and AI, plans for some broadening, and hedges war risk with longs in crude and equity vol.
Midterm election risk: some point to an AI sell-off in the event of a Blue Wave, and Market Intel would buy dips. Prediction markets show Dems at 66% (Polymarket) and 64% (Kalshi) for the Senate.
If Trump moves back to negotiations rather than kinetic action on Iran, Market Intel expects a broad rally led by Tech and Cyclicals ex-Energy.
Last week the Recession L/S basket (JPRECES) returned 3.4% and the Stagflation L/S basket (JP9STAGP) returned 1.5%, despite lower 1Y and 2Y inflation breakevens and bond yields.

UK Budget was largely in line. The OBR cut fiscal headroom to £15B from £24B and raised net borrowing forecasts by £65B. UK homebuilders fell 6.2% on the lack of detail on a first-time buyer plan. ECB is expected to hold on Thursday.
Bank of Canada hiked to 2.5% and said more could be needed (news link).

earnings_insights: MSFT (reported 10/28 after close): Azure beat buyside estimates by 1 point, operating income beat buyside by +5%, shares +5% after hours.
GOOGL (reported 10/28 after close): Search missed buyside by -2%, YouTube, Cloud revenue and consolidated operating income missed buyside, Cloud operating margins strong, shares -7% after hours.
NOW (reported 10/28 after close): CRPO missed buyside estimates, Q4 CRPO guide implies -250bp sequential deceleration, shares -15% after hours.
ADP (reported 10/28): fiscal Q1 pays per control growth 2%, ahead of expectations. Fiscal 2027 outlook raised to about 1% from 0-1%.
GEV (reported 10/28): about $30bn of new orders in Q3, backlog up from $176bn to about $200bn.
VRT (reported 10/28): Q3 data center orders up more than 100% Y/Y organically, EMEA pipeline about doubled Y/Y.
CHRW (reported 10/28): average headcount down 10.4% Y/Y in Q3 and down 2% sequentially, absorbing about $30M of annual wage inflation.
ODFL (reported 10/28): Q3 average headcount down 4% versus a 2% decrease in shipments per day, wage increase of 3%-3.5%, fringe benefit rate 42.8% vs 39.7% a year ago.
SK Hynix (reported 10/28): big beat with longer demand visibility.
Upcoming 10/29 after close: AMZN, COIN, INTC, MSTR, SBUX, PINS, RBLX, FSLR, GILD. Before open: LLY, MRK, CAT, MA, BMY, LIN.

trade_ideas.rationale: Consumer momentum is building, seasonality is supportive, positioning is under-owned and midterms could be an incremental catalyst.

trade_ideas.description: Midterm election asymmetry: short Federal Gov Contractors ex Defense (JPUXFEDB), long Affordable Care Act Exchange Levered (JPUXACA)
trade_ideas.rationale: Divided government lowers legislative productivity and raises federal funding risk, while gridlock could put ACA subsidies back on the table.

trade_ideas.description: Long crude and Energy equities plus long equity vol as a hedge against Middle East war risk, alongside long Tech / AI
trade_ideas.rationale: Primary risk is a spike in kinetic conflict in the Middle East.
trade_ideas.risk: Conflict resolution or a move back to negotiations would remove the hedge's value.

risk_factors: Spike in kinetic conflict in the Middle East, especially strikes on Saudi and UAE energy infrastructure with the SPR at multi-decade lows.
Midterm elections on Nov 3, with some pointing to an AI sell-off in a Blue Wave.
Input cost and wage inflation, including healthcare and benefits costs.
Elevated energy costs from oil, natural gas and diesel.
Hot GOOGL and NOW prints may signal AI-related stock sensitivity to misses.
Elevated mortgage rates and consumer stress.
vol_and_positioning: Sentiment is firmly in the Fear region (CNN index) but a complete positioning washout has not occurred.
Market Intel suggests hedging war risk with longs in crude and equity vol.
NOW sentiment going into the print was a touch long.
Holiday spend basket thesis: positioning is under-owned and recent gains came from short covering rather than broad long exposure.
geopolitical: Iran: Trump said he is nearing a decision on negotiation or continued attacks, with a third aircraft carrier nearing the region. Iran said any new bombing would lead it to target the region, including Israel and the UAE.
Chatter of a 3-day war. Iran would likely target Saudi and UAE energy infrastructure while the SPR is at multi-decade lows.
Worst case is Russian refining capacity being hit again.
Expiration of the Trump-Xi one-year trade truce on Nov 1, with a separate item noting an extension through Jan 20, 2027.
UK Budget leaves pressure on the BoE for rate hikes.
World Bank sees commodity prices up 23% in 2026 due to Middle East war and other shocks (news link).
